blocks.text: 1. Residual Connections
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445885909-685264967.png

Embeddings, the previous topic, explained how discrete tokens become continuous vectors. Residual Connections take a closer, dedicated look at the skip connections used throughout every Transformer sublayer, explored throughout this topic.
They work by adding a sublayer's own input directly to its own output, exactly the idea already previewed in Transformer Architecture, now explored in complete depth throughout this topic.
2. Recapping ResNet's Own Innovation

This connects back to skip connections, already covered in ResNet. ResNet genuinely introduced this idea to train dramatically deeper Convolutional Neural Networks, already covered there in that earlier context.
This topic genuinely explores exactly how that same idea applies within the Transformer, directly reusing a technique already proven valuable in a completely different architectural family.

This is a genuinely consistent pattern repeated throughout both the encoder and decoder, both already covered, applied identically at every single sublayer throughout the entire architecture.

blocks.text: 4. Why Transformers Need This Especially
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445885910-504690791.png

This connects back to why skip connections genuinely help, already covered in ResNet. A genuinely deep stack of encoder and decoder layers, already covered in Transformer Architecture, faces the exact same degradation risk already covered there.

Residual connections genuinely keep this genuinely deep architecture trainable, directly applying the exact same fix already covered for ResNet's own genuinely deep design to this genuinely different architecture family.
5. The Gradient Flow Benefit
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445885910-621058704.png

This connects back to why skip connections genuinely help with gradients, already covered in ResNet. Gradients genuinely flow directly backward through each residual connection, exactly as already covered there.

This bypasses the vanishing gradient risk already covered generally throughout this course, giving the Transformer's own genuinely deep stack of layers a genuinely reliable path for gradients to travel.

blocks.text: 6. Recapping The Identity Mapping Ease

This connects back to the ease of learning an identity mapping, already covered in ResNet. If a sublayer genuinely needs to do little or nothing, it can genuinely learn to output values close to zero.

This lets the residual connection genuinely pass information through nearly unchanged, the exact same flexibility already covered for ResNet's own blocks, now available to every single Transformer sublayer too.
7. Always Paired With Normalization
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445885910-350535068.png
This connects back to Layer Normalization, already covered in the Normalization Techniques module. Residual connections genuinely always pair with Layer Normalization directly afterward.
This is the exact consistent pattern already covered as residual and normalization in The Encoder, applied identically throughout every single sublayer covered throughout this entire module.

blocks.text: 8. Enabling Extreme Depth
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446020358-756020332.png

A genuinely important, real practical consequence connects back to extreme depth achieved, already covered in ResNet. Modern Transformers genuinely stack dozens or even hundreds of layers, relying directly on residual connections to remain trainable.

This genuinely dramatic scale, already covered in this section, directly parallels the extreme depth already covered as ResNet's own significant achievement, now realized within the Transformer architecture family too.
9. Recognizing Why Residual Connections Are Genuinely Non-Negotiable

blocks.alt: Recognizing Why Residual Connections Are Genuinely Non-Negotiable
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446020360-392584197.png
This connects back to enabling extreme depth, already covered in this topic. Without them, already covered, genuinely deep Transformer stacks would likely become genuinely untrainable.
Building any genuinely deep, stacked Attention-based architecture is another genuine case where residual connections, already covered, are genuinely a standard, expected component.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates a genuinely deep stack of layers, contrasting training stability with and without residual connections, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
hidden_size = 8
num_layers = 20  # a genuinely deep stack, already covered as enabling extreme depth in this topic

def sublayer(x, rng):
    W = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.05  # deliberately small, under-trained weights
    return np.tanh(x @ W)

def stack_without_residual(x, num_layers, rng):
    for _ in range(num_layers):
        x = sublayer(x, rng)  # already covered as the degradation risk in this topic
    return x

def stack_with_residual(x, num_layers, rng):
    for _ in range(num_layers):
        x = x + sublayer(x, rng)  # already covered as a residual connection in this topic
    return x

input_signal = rng.normal(size=hidden_size)

output_without_residual = stack_without_residual(input_signal.copy(), num_layers, rng)
output_with_residual = stack_with_residual(input_signal.copy(), num_layers, rng)

print(f"Input magnitude: {np.linalg.norm(input_signal):.4f}")
print(f"Output magnitude without residual connections: {np.linalg.norm(output_without_residual):.4f}")
print(f"Output magnitude with residual connections: {np.linalg.norm(output_with_residual):.4f}")
print("\nNotice the residual version genuinely preserves more of the original signal, already covered as the identity mapping ease in this topic")

blocks.content: Running this example across a genuinely deep, 20-layer stack shows the residual version genuinely preserving more of the original signal's magnitude, exactly the identity mapping ease already covered as this topic's own core benefit.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Residual Connections add a sublayer's own input directly to its own output.
This directly reuses the skip connection idea already covered in ResNet.
Every sublayer, Self-Attention, Cross-Attention, and the feed-forward network, gets wrapped in one.
A deep stack of Transformer layers faces the same degradation risk already covered in ResNet.
Gradients flow directly backward through each residual connection, bypassing vanishing gradients.
A sublayer needing little change can learn near-zero output, passing information through nearly unchanged.
Residual connections always pair with Layer Normalization directly afterward.
They enable modern Transformers to stack dozens or hundreds of layers while remaining trainable.
